pr_title: reverseproxy: Pick the least loaded host in random_choose when all are busy
pr_body:
Closes #8158

`leastRequests` kept every earlier candidate when it found a host with fewer active requests. So once no host was idle, `random_choose` chose at random between the most and the least loaded hosts. It now starts the candidate list over when it finds a strictly smaller count, and only adds hosts that tie with the best count.

Test: `TestLeastRequestsAllBusy` gives three hosts 30, 1 and 20 active requests and expects the host with 1 every time. Without the change it returns the host with 30 about half the time; with it, always the host with 1. `go test ./...` passes.

Manual check with the Caddyfile from the issue (slow and fast backend, 80 requests): v2.11.7 sent 39 to the slow one and 41 to the fast one. With the change it sent 10 and 70, about the same as `least_conn` (11 and 69).

## Assistance Disclosure

Claude Code (Claude Opus) helped write this patch and its test. I reviewed every line, and I ran the test before and after the change and the manual check above myself.

task_text:
# reverseproxy: random_choose picks the busier host half the time once no upstream is idle

### Issue Details

`lb_policy random_choose 2` is meant to pick two upstreams at random and send the request to the less loaded one. That only works while one of the two has 0 requests in flight. Once both are busy, which is the normal state under load, it picks between them at random, so it behaves like `lb_policy random`.

Version: v2.11.7 (release binary) and master at 700d6032.

Caddyfile, with a slow backend on :9011 (3 s per response) and a fast one on :9012 (0.3 s):

```
{
	admin off
	auto_https off
}
:9010 {
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:9011 127.0.0.1:9012 {
		lb_policy random_choose 2
	}
}
```

Sending 80 requests 50 ms apart:

```
random_choose 2: slow=39  fast=41
least_conn:      slow=11  fast=69
```

Expected: `random_choose 2` with two upstreams should match `least_conn`, since both are always candidates.

Cause: `leastRequests` in `modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/selectionpolicies.go`. When it finds a host with fewer active requests than the best so far, it appends that host to `best` instead of starting `best` over with it. For hosts with [30, 1] requests, `best` ends up holding both, and one is picked at random. (#7873 fixed the idle-host shortcut above this loop, not this part.)

I have a small patch with a test and can open a PR if this sounds right.

### Assistance Disclosure

AI used

### If AI was used, describe the extent to which it was used.

Claude Code (Claude Opus) helped write the reproduction, the patch and its test. I reviewed every line and re-ran the steps above myself.
